tagline: Ridge crossings and orchard roads link the Rondout and Wallkill valleys.
intro: The Shawangunk Mountains Scenic Byway circles the northern Shawangunks through the Rondout and Wallkill valleys, covering 88 miles. Routes 44/55 cross the mountains with a hairpin, overlooks and a forested descent among glacial boulders and conglomerate rock. The Shawangunk Mountains Regional Partnership says New York State awarded scenic-byway designation for the region’s scenic, natural, historic and recreational resources.

The New Paltz and Wawarsing Turnpike crossed the Trapps in 1857. Investors sought markets for Catskills products, but the turnpike went bankrupt within a few years; Routes 44/55 follow much of its course. Planning for the modern byway took six years and brought nine towns and two villages into an intermunicipal partnership. Their shared purpose was to improve transportation and encourage tourism while preserving the region’s resources. The legislature and governor designated the byway in fall 2006; an alternate route through Gardiner followed in fall 2009.

Begin in Ellenville, where Route 52 climbs into the mountains before descending to Walker Valley and continuing to Pine Bush. The Wallkill Valley route leads onward through Wallkill, past orchards toward Ireland Corners and New Paltz. On the northern loop, Rosendale and High Falls connect with Route 209 through Accord and Kerhonkson. From Route 209, Routes 44/55 cross the ridge again, passing Minnewaska and Mohonk before reaching Gardiner.

moments.title: Ellenville
moments.text: Ellenville’s name emerged from a meeting place: the Hoornbeek Tavern. Nathan and Maria Hoornbeek had enlarged an earlier dwelling into an inn, where residents gathered to make community decisions. When village leaders could not agree on a name, Maria’s sister Ellen Snyder persuaded them to use hers. Charles Hartshorn later built his family home on the tavern’s former site. He also became the first postmaster and, in 1856, the first president of the incorporated village. The village lies at the meeting of Route 52 and US 209, between the western base of the Shawangunk Ridge and the eastern base of the Catskills.

moments.title: Rosendale Trestle
moments.text: The Rosendale Trestle carries a pedestrian walkway 150 feet above Rondout Creek. The Wallkill Valley Railroad built the crossing to extend its line from New Paltz to Kingston; rail traffic began in 1872. Rebuilding in 1895–96 replaced iron and wood with steel. After the railway closed, Conrail sold the bridge to John E. Rahl for one dollar in 1986. His attempt to operate a bungee-jumping platform failed. Following a county tax foreclosure and renovation, the trestle reopened to the public in June 2013. Below the span lie Route 213 and the former Delaware and Hudson Canal.

moments.title: Routes 44/55
moments.text: A notch formed by cross-cutting faults gives Routes 44/55 their passage through the Shawangunks. Approaching from Route 209, the road crosses Rondout Creek and climbs past two overlooks facing the Rondout Valley and Catskill Mountains. The mountain crossing passes the entrances to Minnewaska State Park Preserve and Mohonk’s Trapps area. On the eastern side, an overlook faces the Wallkill Valley, and the road bends through a five-mile-per-hour hairpin near the Trapps Gateway Visitor Center. The full route between Route 209 and Ireland Corners covers 16.4 miles. Toward Gardiner, a steel bridge takes the road across the Wallkill River.
moments.notice: The overlooks face the Wallkill Valley on one side and the Rondout Valley and Catskills on the other.
